title: Why does a skyscraper hang a giant golden ball?
description:
He hung a giant golden ball inside his skinny tower and everyone laughed. Then the wind came: a short rope, a rival with a winch, and one swing that explains it all.

This is a made-up story (Pete, Rex and the town are invented). The idea is real: a heavy mass hung on a long enough rope inside a tall building swings against the sway and soaks it up. It is called a tuned mass damper, and Taipei 101 has a steel ball of about 660 tonnes hanging between its 87th and 92nd floors to do exactly that.
